gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '2.5 hr' battery figures for the MoGo 4, MoGo 4 Laser, Mars 3 Air and GV50 are Eco-mode ratings at reduced brightness. Tested at full brightness, these projectors ran 86–113 minutes. The one test of a Mars 3 Air in Eco mode (ProjectorCentral) measured 145 lumens, against 383 at full power. The Nebula Mars 3 is the only candidate that holds about 300 lumens in Eco for its rated 5 hours.
standout_why: The cited rival pages are RTINGS' 'Best Projectors Under $1,000' (2026-10-05) and 'Best Portable Projectors' (2026-10-16). I fetched both, but their review text did not load (the pages build it with JavaScript), so I could not check the picks' runtime or brightness figures against them. I did not open the uncited top results (What Hi-Fi?, Esquire, Wirecutter and others). Treat the comparison with rivals as unconfirmed. ChatGPT's own answer puts '2.5 hrs' against four projectors as if the figures were the same. It flags only the Mars 3's figure as Eco. It does not say that the other 2.5-hour ratings are also Eco or reduced-brightness figures, or what brightness is left in that mode.
decides: For backyard or camping use on battery alone, this changes the pick. The Mars 3 Air's 2.5 hours (Eco) came with 145 lumens measured in Eco. The Mars 3 measured 298 lumens in Eco (Standard picture mode), and Anker rates it for 5 hours in Eco. That is about twice the light for twice the rated time, so the Mars 3 is the battery pick despite its weight. For a bedroom where the projector stays plugged in, it confirms ChatGPT's picks: a full-brightness movie on battery alone will not reach 2 hours on the MoGo 4, MoGo 4 Laser or GV50, so plan on the outlet, the $129 XGIMI PowerBase, or for the GV50 a USB-C power bank above 65 W. Price correction: the MoGo 4 Laser alone is $669 at XGIMI's US store. ChatGPT's $749 is the price of the 'Outdoor Collection' bundle.
